title: Tenant-weighted interrupt scheduler with hotset safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a tenant-weighted interruptible scheduler for continuous batching that preserves per-tenant latency SLOs while protecting KV cache hotsets and minimizing GPU memory churn. Motivation: current preemption heuristics are coarse and cause excessive KV eviction or full-model GPU compaction during interrupt cycles, increasing tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants and reducing overall throughput. Scope: 1) design scheduling policy that allocates interrupt budgets proportional to tenant SLO slack and recent token/sequence distributions; 2) introduce a hotset-insulation mechanism to reserve small KV cache slices for tenants with frequent short-sequence traffic; 3) add an opportunistic GPU compaction window that only runs when predicted benefit exceeds measured interruption overhead. Acceptance criteria: - 95th percentile latency for P0 tenants preserved within 1.2x of baseline under mixed workloads; - effective KV hotset hit-rate uplift of >=8% for protected tenants during preemption events; - GPU memory compaction overhead <5% additional tail latency overall; - rollout flag and telemetry with per-tenant SLO signal, preempt counts, KV eviction events, compaction triggers. Design notes: - Scheduler computes a per-tenant interrupt budget proportional to max(1, floor(weight * SLO_slack_score)) where weight = committed share + recent 'short-job' factor. - Interrupts are ordered by (priority, estimated remaining tokens, kv_hotness_penalty) to prefer yielding long low-priority batches while keeping hot KV sets intact. - Hotset insulation: assign small KV slabs (configurable per-tenant) pinned in GPU memory; these slabs are accounted separately and not reclaimed during normal preemption; eviction of insulated slabs requires explicit high-priority global compaction or admin override. - GPU compaction: run asynchronously in small windows triggered only when free_memory_fraction < threshold AND predicted future eviction cost > compaction_cost. - Fallback: when insulated slabs cause memory pressure, the scheduler will probabilistically throttle incoming low-priority requests rather than evict insulated KV entries. Trade-offs considered: - Reserving KV slabs improves short-tail latencies but reduces total available cache capacity; we expect better user-facing latency at modest throughput cost. - Conservative compaction avoids repeated compactions but may temporarily increase memory pressure; the prediction model needs a light-weight estimator to avoid adding CPU overhead. Security/model-safety: ensure tenant isolation of KV slabs and audit logs for any forced eviction/compaction. Ops: feature gated behind runtime-1.20 flag; metric dashboards and alerts required before canary rollout.

Early results: 95p latency for P0 tenants reduced by ~15% vs current preemptor under synthetic mixed load. Next: integrate GPU compaction estimator and add telemetry hooks.
